Topics Amazon Apple Black Friday Gadgets Kitchen.

Industry observers note that this year, Black Friday falls on Nov. 27. While retailers often start featuring their best markdowns on Black Friday itself, there are plenty of early deals worth shopping in the lead-up. Most retailers' official sales do start well before the big day, so shopping strategically ahead of time can save you from missing out on a deal entirely (or dealing with the chaos the day after Thanksgiving).

Cyber Monday takes place on the Monday following Thanksgiving. This year, the shopping event takes place on Monday, Nov. 30. While Cyber Monday originally began as an online counterpart to in-person shopping on Black Friday, the two events have merged into an extended online shopping bonanza.

The mega-retailer just wrapped up its October Prime Day sale, and naturally, it's also getting in on the Black Friday action. For 2026, Amazon's official Black Friday sales kicked off on Nov. 19, which means deals are already live. Amazon has an incentive to spread out the shopping (to give its delivery drivers a break), so you no longer have to wait until Thanksgiving to save. Deals will continue to go live through Nov. 30.

Amazon: Amazon recently announced that its Black Friday sale will begin on Nov. 19, with newly introduced deals dropping through Cyber Monday, on Nov. 30.

According to recent reports, best Buy: The massive box store is hosting its Early Black Friday Deals + Doorbusters sale from Nov. 6 through Nov. 18, and the official Best Buy Black Friday sale kicks off on Nov. 19 and runs through Nov. 28. The Best Buy Cyber Monday Sale Event runs for 48 hours on Nov. 29 and Nov. 30.

Walmart: Walmart has three major sale events throughout November: the early Black Friday sale from Nov. 12 to Nov. 15, the Black Friday sale from Nov. 23 to Nov. 29 (with deals online only from Nov. 23 to Nov. 26), and the online-only Cyber Monday sale from Nov. 30 to Dec. 2.

Industry observers note that target: Target hasn't released its full Black Friday lineup yet, but we do know its first Early Black Friday sale kicks off Nov. 5 to Nov. 7. From Nov. 1 to Dec. 24, Target's Deal of the Day offer kicks off, featuring new deals every day. Every weekend after Nov. 7, the retailer will also drop new limited-time holiday offers.

In a recent development, the Home Depot: The Home Depot's main Black Friday sale runs from Nov. 5 to Nov. 25, wrapping up a bit earlier than other big retailers. However, the home improvement store will continue to offer upcoming deals throughout November, and its Cyber Week sale kicks off on Nov. 30 and runs through Dec. 6.

Uber and Nuro begin driverless testing of Lucid robotaxis ahead of 2027 launch

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Uber and Nuro have started testing driverless Lucid Gravity SUVs on public streets in the San Francisco Bay Area more than six months after receiving the permit that allowed the companies to pull the human safety driver from behind the wheel.
  • The companies will soon begin offering driverless rides to employees in the final lead-up to launching a commercial robotaxi service in the first quarter of 2027.
  • The milestone comes just 16 months after Uber announced an ambitious plan to launch a premium robotaxi service using Lucid electric vehicles outfitted with autonomous vehicle technology developed by startup Nuro.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Uber and Nuro have started testing driverless Lucid Gravity SUVs on public streets in the San Francisco Bay Area more than six months after receiving the permit that allowed the companies to pull the human safety driver from behind the wheel.

The companies will soon begin offering driverless rides to employees in the final lead-up to launching a commercial robotaxi service in the first quarter of 2027.

The milestone comes just 16 months after Uber announced an ambitious plan to launch a premium robotaxi service using Lucid electric vehicles outfitted with autonomous vehicle technology developed by startup Nuro.

That initiative came with hefty investments in both companies and much-needed endorsements of their respective products. Uber initially agreed to invest $300 million in Lucid — a figure that has since ballooned to $500 million. Uber also agreed to invest nearly $500 million in Nuro, TechCrunch previously reported, citing sources familiar with the deal.

The agreement provided both Lucid and Nuro with boosts beyond the obvious capital injection. Uber agreed to buy at least 20,000 of Lucid Gravity SUVs over the next six years (a figure that later popped to at least 35,000 vehicles), giving the struggling EV maker a more predictable source of revenue. Nuro, meanwhile, was less than a year removed from announcing a risky, but necessary pivot away from developing driverless delivery vehicles and toward licensing its autonomous vehicle technology to automakers and mobility companies.

Nuro has spent nearly a year testing the Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area with a human safety operator behind the wheel. The California Department of Motor Vehicles, the agency that regulates the testing and deployment of autonomous vehicles in the state, granted Nuro a driverless AV permit in May 2026.

Uber and Nuro are also testing autonomous vehicles on public roads in Houston with human safety operators behind the wheel. Nuro is supplementing that on-road testing with closed-course testing and simulation to validate the self-driving system before opening the robotaxis to the public. The companies’ combined engineering fleet of autonomous vehicles, which stood at 100 AVs earlier this year, is expanding as Lucid begins manufacturing the first production versions of the robotaxis at its Arizona factory.

Industry observers note that the Lucid Gravity robotaxi, unveiled in January 2026, is outfitted with high-resolution cameras, solid-state lidar sensors, and radars that help the self-driving system perceive the real-world environment and operate in it. Uber, which will own and operate the fleet, has focused its efforts on the in-cabin experience, including how riders will interact with the vehicle.

#116860. The biggest limitations of ChatGPT

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (530 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

The biggest limitations of ChatGPT

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (530 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • From fabricated citations to forgotten instructions, ChatGPT still has some frustrating blind spots.
  • Industry observers note that it's no secret that ChatGPT can write up emails, become your software troubleshooter and even dumb down complicated questions in an instant.
  • According to recent reports, some shortcomings are tied to the model or version of it that you're using, along with any plugins you've added.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From fabricated citations to forgotten instructions, ChatGPT still has some frustrating blind spots.

Industry observers note that it's no secret that ChatGPT can write up emails, become your software troubleshooter and even dumb down complicated questions in an instant. But it's also pretty capable of making up responses so polished that you might not think to verify the shaky facts behind them. If only most of us had the confidence that ChatGPT has when it is hallucinating. Even after OpenAI brought its advanced GPT-6 model to all ChatGPT consumers in October 2026, the chatbot still has the tendency to fabricate supporting evidence, misread an ambiguous question and even forget instructions amid a lengthy conversation.

According to recent reports, some shortcomings are tied to the model or version of it that you're using, along with any plugins you've added. And just because you're paying for ChatGPT Plus or the $100 ChatGPT Pro proposal doesn't mean you're guarded against the chatbot's biggest limitations. To be fair, this isn't a problem unique to OpenAI, as most of these shortcomings are common in AI assistants we compared, like Claude.

Topping the list of ChatGPT's biggest quirks is its bad habit of hallucinating, or crafting details that seem legitimate but are entirely made up. Packing all the confidence of a subject-matter expert, ChatGPT will cite studies that don't exist and make them almost believable with imaginary quotations too.

Recent findings suggest that openAI is quite upfront about this and warns that ChatGPT could invent quotes and cite fake sources. Using ChatGPT Search does make things better, but just because the response has some live links doesn't make the final statement correct. While an expert on the topic could probably catch the counterfeit sources upon closer inspection, this could be troublesome for someone looking for references in uncharted territory.

Sources indicate that chatGPT can also follow detailed instructions and acknowledge a mistake you've pointed out, only to ignore it a few prompts later. One user on OpenAI's community forum reported that ChatGPT reused earlier details in a report and presented them as verified, then repeated the mistake after admitting it.

In a recent development, but then, that's one person's experience and not exactly strong evidence of this being a problem across the board. That said, researchers found that the reliability of language models tends to go down as input length increases, even if the tasks aren't inherently complex. The researchers tested 18 different models, using older versions of OpenAI's GPT, Google's Gemini and Anthropic's Claude, so the findings may not be an accurate depiction of how GPT-6 performs. And just because you've fed your AI model an enormous amount of context doesn't guarantee it will make the most of it.

Recent findings suggest that if you're working on a lengthy project across several days, being mindful of the changes requested and repeating the given instructions is part of the play. Sure, it can get frustrating that a tool that should be saving you time needs so much babysitting, but the alternative is far more time- and labor-intensive. OpenAI also acknowledges that ChatGPT's Memory feature doesn't retain every detail from every conversation anyway.

Kalshi makes “difficult decision” to halt Utah trading after losing court fights

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1388 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kalshi made the “difficult decision” to pause operations in Utah after losing a court fight to block the state’s ongoing enforcement actions under Utah gambling laws, Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick said Monday.
  • Industry observers note that it seems Kalshi’s legal troubles in Utah have become too much for the prediction market platform to gamble on continued operations there.
  • Kalshi also wasn’t saved by an emergency motion from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission—which argues that the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction market trading.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kalshi made the “difficult decision” to pause operations in Utah after losing a court fight to block the state’s ongoing enforcement actions under Utah gambling laws, Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick said Monday.

Industry observers note that it seems Kalshi’s legal troubles in Utah have become too much for the prediction market platform to gamble on continued operations there. In Utah, several lawsuits are still playing out, and Kalshi also lost a bid to persuade a federal appeals court to block those cases until the appeal is resolved.

Kalshi also wasn’t saved by an emergency motion from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission—which argues that the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction market trading. At this time, the federal district court has not granted that motion to block Utah’s enforcement actions, either.

“This is an unfortunate outcome for the more than 177,000 Utahns who use Kalshi,” McGavick mentioned. “We will continue to fight this in court, and we look forward to returning to Utah once our legal position is vindicated.”.

Utah’s attorney general, Derek Brown, had filed both civil and criminal charges against Kalshi, as he defended the state’s 130-year ban on gambling.

It has been revealed that in a press release discussing the initial lawsuit, he accused Kalshi of running “an online casino” that violates the state’s constitution. “Not only do our state laws ban gambling but Utah is one of only two states where gambling is also prohibited under the state constitution,” Brown noted. “For 130 years, Utah has been clear: gambling has no place here, and we will enforce our laws.”.

Late Monday, a major Utah-area news outlet, KSL.com, reported that Brown was prepared to jail Kalshi’s co-founders, who had been summoned to be booked on 14 charges on December 5. He defended those intends, saying, “There is a question I have seen from people asking, ‘Well, do we modify this booking process if someone is a very wealthy and well-known tech billionaire?’ and the answer is ‘No, the process is the process; we don’t modify it based on who you are.’”.

According to recent reports, however, on Tuesday, Utah decided to drop the criminal charges against Kalshi, McGavick confirmed to Ars. In a statement on X, Kalshi general counsel Yaakov Roth noted, “We are pleased that Utah has chosen to dismiss criminal charges against Kalshi, while proceeding with civil litigation. Good faith jurisdictional disagreements should never be criminalized. We stand ready to work with State AGs on reasonable interim measures until courts resolve the dispute over who regulates prediction markets.”.

In a press release, Brown explained that the charges were dropped specifically due to the pause.

Industry observers note that “Kalshi said it would geofence Utah, which blocks access to its site in the state,” the press release said. “The company also committed to monitor for Utah-based IP addresses trying to reach its site. The Office then reevaluated its position and moved to dismiss the criminal case against the company and the individual defendants.”.

Brown threatened that the charges would be raised again if Kalshi tried to renew operations.

In a recent development, “Utah does not allow gambling, and prediction markets are gambling,” Brown said. Kalshi has pulled out of Utah, and if it returns, so will the charges. Every organization in this space should take note. If they promote, support, or enable gambling, we will hold them accountable.”.

Discussion of the Kalshi pause in a Utah sub-Reddit found some Redditors skeptical of the state’s cases as potentially overreaching.

However, many top commenters seemed pleased with the enforcement efforts, suggesting that Utah may have bipartisan support among some residents. One commenter cheered on the attorney general’s efforts as “the one item in the Utah GOP’s agenda I can get behind,” while another agreed that “prediction markets are incredibly toxic and are manipulated against ordinary people.”.

Recent findings suggest that many complained that Kalshi ads flooded their social media feeds. Some suggested the state should focus on banning advertising of prediction markets, while potentially still allowing adults to trade on event contracts if they want to throw their “money away.”.

It has been revealed that fears of insider trading were also raised. One commenter laid out why prediction markets seem suspiciously designed to promote insider trading and other market manipulation:.

Industry observers note that “I’m pretty libertarian and hate banning things. But gambling and prediction markets are a scourge. Even the term ‘prediction market’ is a misnomer. Because ultimately when people with substantial dollars get involved it creates a financial incentive for them to make fucked up things happen in the real world. Think about it, decades ago we understood that sports betting was a problem because it corrupted sports—something that ultimately is pretty meaningless. Then we got all these people betting on the stock market with puts and it created huge incentives to cause havoc with markets. Now if people are betting big money on politics and wars and everything else, it just means people with influence can make money by making improbable/unexpected things happen.”.

Industry observers note that one commenter joked, “I wonder how Kashi would have reacted if the judge in charge of their case had ‘traded’ $500,000 on the event of them losing the case. Not a problem at all, right?”.

On the same day Kalshi confirmed its temporary pause in Utah, a judge rejected a request from New York Attorney General Letitia James to immediately shut down Kalshi in that state, Courthouse News reported.

Upcoming York Supreme Court Justice Melissa Crane stated she was “uncomfortable” granting the temporary restraining order so early in the case because “there does seem to be an indication that there would be market disruption that I’m concerned about.” Kalshi attorney Grant Mainland described it a little differently, claiming that a sudden halt would cause a “market emergency.”.

Industry observers note that “I think this is the ultimate relief in the case, which is improper for me to do without full briefing,” Crane said. Instead of granting James’ request, she recommended that Kalshi take steps to address the state’s top concerns by considering “safeguards for people between 18 and 20,” who are under the state’s legal gambling age, Courthouse News reported.

According to Kalshi’s estimates, Upcoming York’s Kalshi user base (1.5 million) is much larger than Utah’s, so the market disruption from the Utah shutdown may not have carried the same dire stakes for Kalshi or its broader user base.

The CFTC has sought to intervene in that case, too, and it seems clear that Kalshi expects the questions of who can regulate prediction markets and what trading qualifies as a “bet” to reach the Supreme Court. Kalshi’s spokesperson did not respond to Ars’ questions on how the Utah pause broadly impacted owners or the platform.

So far, “three federal appeals courts have ruled that states can regulate prediction markets, while a fourth found they cannot,” Courthouse News reported. But despite the current balance tipping toward allowing states to regulate prediction markets, Kalshi appears confident that the Supreme Court will resolve the disparate court rulings in its favor.

In a lawsuit filed by a disgruntled Kalshi user, Kalshi argued that it would waste lower courts’ time to continue litigating these cases and that no case should be resolved until the Supreme Court weighs in.

In that case, Kalshi user Scott Bright alleged that he lost more than $300,000 on sports bets that were technically illegal in Washington.

According to Kalshi, all of Bright’s claims rest “on the premise that state gambling laws reach KalshiEX’s federally regulated exchange—the question now before the Supreme Court. Plaintiff puts the cart before the horse; Defendants ask only that the Court let that threshold question be resolved first.”.

The court has yet to address Kalshi’s request to stay the case, but Bright has argued that Kalshi is trying to “sideline a case governed by binding Ninth Circuit precedent so that they can wait for a Supreme Court decision that may never come.”.

Kalshi did not respond to Ars’ request for a statement on Bright’s lawsuit. In their court filing, they argued that “a stay will let the Supreme Court address an matter that could dispose of every claim, will not meaningfully harm Plaintiff, and will spare Defendants and the Court litigation under a framework that may soon be displaced.”.

Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (536 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Music streaming service Tidal mentioned on Tuesday that it will start banning and removing songs generated fully with AI in a bid to stem the flood of submissions to its platform.
  • Tidal remarked it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year.
  • Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata says they are made fully using AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Music streaming service Tidal mentioned on Tuesday that it will start banning and removing songs generated fully with AI in a bid to stem the flood of submissions to its platform. The firm said that over the past 90 days, more than 43% of tracks uploaded to its platform were generated by AI, and that was a major reason driving this decision.

Tidal remarked it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year. With the fresh rules in place, the platform said it will be rejecting roughly 80,000-85,000 tracks per day.

Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata says they are made fully using AI.

The tech giant stated it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.

The move comes as AI-generated music inundates streaming services across the board. Tidal is one of the first major platforms after Bandcamp to ban AI music outright. Deezer, which also provides detection tools to other streaming services, stated that it will introduce a toggle to let owners filter out AI music. Larger platforms like Spotify and YouTube Music have adopted a milder approach to this glitch, choosing to label AI-generated music instead of offering filters or taking stronger measures.

Tidal started de-monetizing songs made using AI in June, but that did not prove enough of a deterrent, Tidal Music’s lead, Robert Anderson, remarked on X.

In a recent development, A few months ago, @Tidal tagged and demonetized all wholly AI-generated tracks to protect the authenticity of real artists. But that’s enough, as 43% of tracks distributed to us in the last 90 days have been detected as AI-generated. Something more drastic needs to be done….

The manufacturer said that 27 million, or 6.3% of tracks on the platform, are fully AI-generated, but 96% of those have no streams.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, music labels are trying to make money by partnering with platforms and AI model makers to sell their catalog for training or remixing features. Goldman Sachs estimates that by 2035, AI-related licensing tools and latest monetization opportunities have the potential to improve record labels’ revenue by 10%.

Britons get many of the facts about migration wrong and Reform UK voters are the group who get these facts most wrong, according to newly introduced research published today by King’s College University and YouGov.

#116850. Why you should never reply with STOP when you receive spam texts

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (874 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Why you should never reply with STOP when you receive spam texts

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (874 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An honest opt-out method for marketing messages sends a different signal to shady scammers.
  • Industry observers note that you've likely noticed the "STOP to cancel" note when you receive texts from short codes.
  • Nobody wants garbage texts about phony job offers, illicit encounters or other scams, but it's vital to think carefully about how you respond to them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An honest opt-out method for marketing messages sends a different signal to shady scammers.

Industry observers note that you've likely noticed the "STOP to cancel" note when you receive texts from short codes. And for legitimate communications that you asked to receive from restaurants, surveys, loyalty programs and similar, STOP is a fine way to cut them off. But it's not your only option for ending unwanted texts, and for many kinds, it can do more harm than good.

Nobody wants garbage texts about phony job offers, illicit encounters or other scams, but it's vital to think carefully about how you respond to them. Rather than deleting them and dealing with more in the future, you have other options — and they're ones that won't prompt more incoming junk.

Remember to treat any messages from unknown numbers with caution, since they're used for "wrong number" scams and all kinds of other schemes. Don't tap an unexpected link, even if it claims you have an unpaid toll or need to confirm details to fix a delivery problem.

It has been revealed that however, not all the texts you get from unknown numbers are like this. Spam texts that advertise lonely singles, too-good-to-be-true job offers, package delivery scams or other types of nonsense aren't operating within normal marketing laws. You might thus reply STOP out of habit, even if they don't include a note about that.

By doing so, you're confirming to the sender that your number is active, which will likely result in you getting even more junk texts. It costs spammers almost nothing to send out many thousands of texts to random numbers, but few of those are confirmed as live, so you're making yourself a target. Replying can also demonstrate that you aren't able to recognize a text scam, possibly tagging you for future efforts if they think they can hook you.

Industry observers note that only reply STOP when you want to stop getting alerts you specifically signed up for. For anything else, never respond; instead, you should use your phone's tools to deal with unwanted messages safely.

It has been revealed that on iPhone, you should see a Stop or Report Spam button under messages from unknown senders that include a STOP note. Tap this, and you can choose Delete and Stop or Delete and Report Spam. Both erase the conversation from your phone; the former sends a STOP reply after doing this, while the latter reports the message to your carrier and Apple. For messages without a mention of STOP, the only option is Report Spam.

A similar option appears at the bottom of conversations with unknown senders; tap Delete followed by Delete and Report Spam. In case the number keeps contacting you, tap the number at the top of the conversation and choose Block Contact to cut off all communication.

According to recent reports, on Android, you can report an entire conversation as spam in Google Messages by holding it in the list, then choosing Block > Report spam. Alternatively, open a conversation, tap the three-dot More button, then choose Details > Block & report spam. You'll also have the option to block the number.

For either platform, you can also long-press the message and forward it to 7726 (SPAM on a keypad). This reports the text to your carrier for analysis, helping it block spammers across the network. You might get a response asking for the sender's number, so wait to block it until you've confirmed this.

Even when you know what to do upon receiving junk texts, it's better if you don't get them in the first place. Android and iOS both have ways to filter low-quality messages so you aren't getting alerted for nothing.

If you have an iPhone, visit Settings > Apps > Messages, where you have a few choices. Turn on Filter Spam to send obvious garbage to a separate Spam folder. Enable Screen Unknown Senders, then messages from numbers not in your contacts will go to their own folder. And under Text Message Filter, enable the built-in Text Message Filter to put other texts into groups like Transactions and Promotions.

In a recent development, the Allow Notifications menu controls which of these groups send you alerts. Some third-party iPhone apps offer their own message filtering options, which will appear here. Once it's all set up, access the filtered groups from the three-line Filter button at the top-right corner of Messages.

It has been revealed that on Android, open Google Messages, tap your profile picture at the top-right corner and choose Messages settings. Choose Protection & Safety, then you can choose from Standard protection or Enhanced protection for junk messages. In your profile picture menu, choose Spam & blocked to review filtered messages.

Industry observers note that many mobile carriers offer their own protections from spam messages (like T-Mobile ScamShield), which are worth a look if you're still receiving trash. Depending on your carrier, you might activate this by changing a toggle in your account, dialing a code to activate or installing a separate app. The base features should be free; it's almost certainly not worth paying for any premium subscriptions on offer. Third-party tools like Truecaller are another option.

German firms eye Africa as global trade shocks hit traditional markets

💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Africa is a land of opportunity." "The German-African relationship is a win-win." "The continent is the market of the future.".
  • That's what many business leaders and politicians have to say about Africa at the sixth edition of the German-African Business Summit in Accra, Ghana.
  • German firms are increasingly viewing Africa as an attractive destination as they scramble to find fresh markets amid wars in Ukraine and Iran, high energy prices, punishing US tariffs and slowing growth in traditional markets like China.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Africa is a land of opportunity." "The German-African relationship is a win-win." "The continent is the market of the future.".

That's what many business leaders and politicians have to say about Africa at the sixth edition of the German-African Business Summit in Accra, Ghana. While these descriptions aren't upcoming, there's a palpable sense of urgency and seriousness this time.

German firms are increasingly viewing Africa as an attractive destination as they scramble to find fresh markets amid wars in Ukraine and Iran, high energy prices, punishing US tariffs and slowing growth in traditional markets like China.

"For a long time, many German companies had a secure source of revenue from the major export markets in North America and China, but the geopolitical ruptures of our time have undermined this certainty," German President Frank-Walter Steimeier said during the event.

"One could also say that it is time for fresh horizons, time to take a closer look at economic opportunities still waiting for us.".

Africa is home to some of the fastest growing economies in the world like Ethiopia and Rwanda. Even as European and other advanced economies contend with declining working-age populations, Africa is expected to add hundreds of millions of workers in the next decades, emerging as a key source of future labor.

Germany has already signed a migration pact with Kenya and is working on one with Ghana as it seeks to attract skilled workers to help ease acute labor shortages in certain sectors at home.

Recent findings suggest that even as Africa remains one of the poorest regions in the world, economic growth in parts of the continent has created a larger and more affluent consumer class over the past three decades. This group is aspirational and a growing source of demand for many of the goods that German firms want to sell, from cars to cosmetics.

The continent, with its mineral wealth and renewable energy potential, is central to European Union efforts to diversify its sources of critical raw materials and reduce reliance on China-dominated supply chains.

It is also playing an increasingly notable role in strengthening the EU's energy security after the bloc phased out most energy imports from Russia.

German firms have committed to invest billions of euros in green hydrogen projects in countries such as Mauritania and Namibia.

Recent findings suggest that "We don't have the capital to develop them [natural resources]. So foreign investors are coming to help us develop those resources. Whilst we are getting jobs and industrialization is taking place, they are also making profits," remarked Amin Amidu Sulemani, energy and infrastructure commissioner at the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

"It's not a relationship where we send raw materials outside of Africa every time, when we can actually process them here," he told DW.

Despite Africa's growing economic appeal, many obstacles to investment remain, including corruption and governance concerns, unreliable energy supplies, foreign exchange risk and poor infrastructure.

African leaders say they are working to address these challenges and improve the ease of doing business.

Yet while German companies have largely remained on the sidelines, competitors from countries such as the UAE, Turkey and India have made significant inroads across the continent.

German firms enjoy a strong reputation in Africa because of their engineering expertise, vocational training programs and long-term industrial investments, which are more likely to create stable jobs than investments in extractive industries.

It has been revealed that however, they have struggled to translate that goodwill into a larger commercial presence. Africa, for instance, accounts for less than 2% of the total foreign investment made by German firms over the past several decades.

It has been revealed that business leaders complain that German firms lack adequate financing and risk protection for projects in Africa. They also criticize excessive bureaucracy and the absence of a coherent German strategy, with engagement fragmented across ministries and agencies.

Industry bodies say German institutions and firms often perceive risks too broadly, treating diverse African markets as if they pose the same level of risk.

"German companies can be a bit more bold and maybe also innovative in the way they approach the continent," Khadi Camara, deputy CEO of the German-African Business Association, told DW. "We see that in the companies that are successful, they don't do business as usual. Every country has its nuances that companies keep in mind and say, okay, this model works here, that model works there.".

The 2026 World Investment Report by UN trade body UNCTAD showed that investors from the Gulf and Asia are becoming key sources of investment in Africa, especially in energy, logistics, real estate and infrastructure.

The UAE has been a major investor in greenfield megaprojects in recent years, including the $34 billion (€31 billion) Infinity Power renewable energy project in Mauritania, the $24 billion Ras El Hikma real estate development project in Egypt and the $6 billion H2 Global Energy hydrogen project in Tunisia.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Business leaders are calling for better financing and guarantees and more risk-sharing and easing of bureaucratic hurdles.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, others, including the German president, are urging German businesses to take on more risk and seize opportunities in Africa. Otherwise, they risk being edged out by foreign rivals.

"Be curious, take risks and invest in our common future," Steinmeier stated.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Instagram customers can now chat with Meta’s AI agent Muse in a DM thread, the manufacturer declared on Tuesday.
  • The new integration gets rid of the need for customers to toggle between Instagram and the Muse app when they want to interact with the AI agent.
  • Consumers can share Instagram posts with Muse and ask it to take action, such as adding a coffee shop to their Mexico City itinerary or finding a Black Friday deal on a pair of shoes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Instagram customers can now chat with Meta’s AI agent Muse in a DM thread, the manufacturer declared on Tuesday. The social media network says users can chat with Muse to get more context about a post, place, or product they come across, or catch up on conversations they may have missed in their other DMs.

The new integration gets rid of the need for customers to toggle between Instagram and the Muse app when they want to interact with the AI agent. It also reflects the growing competition among tech companies to make AI assistants a part of users’ everyday digital lives. By embedding Muse directly into Instagram, Meta is making it easier for users to access the AI agent, while also giving Muse access to a platform where users already discover products, places, and content.

Consumers can share Instagram posts with Muse and ask it to take action, such as adding a coffee shop to their Mexico City itinerary or finding a Black Friday deal on a pair of shoes.

Meta notes that conversations with Muse on Instagram will appear as a side chat in the main Muse app.

Muse in Instagram DMs will begin rolling out on Tuesday for iOS and Android customers in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, and Singapore.

It has been revealed that meta also revealed that consumers can now do more with the posts and reels they’ve bookmarked on Instagram. For example, they can ask Muse to organize their saved content into custom folders, known as Collections. They could also ask Muse to turn a recipe video into a grocery list, turn the travel content from their favorite travel creators into an itinerary for an upcoming trip, or have Muse send them outfit ideas based on fashion reels they’ve collected.

Starting Tuesday, when users save a post on Instagram, they will see a prompt for Muse to organize it for them. This feature is launching in the U.S. and Canada.

In a recent development, meta claims that users remain in control of their Muse experience on Instagram. Nothing is shared, published, or sent without their approval, and they can ask Muse to forget information or undo actions at any time.

#116843. Industry News: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (925 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (925 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people.
  • That’s why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews.
  • In a recent development, as previously reported, the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this “smoke taint” adversely affected not only local wine production, but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant.

That’s why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists.

In a recent development, as previously reported, the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, in 2018, OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper—identified the growing popularity of “dry hopping” (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon.

All beer contains hops, a key flavoring agent that also imparts useful antimicrobial properties. (Beer spoils quickly without them.) Brewers mash and steep grain in hot water, which converts all that starch into sugars. This is traditionally the stage where hops are added to the liquid extract (wort) and boiled to give the beer that hint of bitterness. During the boiling process, a portion of the resins (alpha acids) in hops isomerize into iso-alpha acids. That chemical rearrangement of the molecules is what produces bitterness. Yeast is then added to trigger fermentation, turning the sugars into alcohol.

In a recent development, far from being the chemically inert ingredient brewers have long assumed, hops contain starch enzymes that, under certain conditions, can boost their activity to such a great extent that excessive re-fermentation occurs (“hop-creep”) after bottling. Dry-hopped beers produce significantly higher CO2 levels and packaging pressures, because there is much more re-fermentation going on than usual. And sometimes that pressure builds until the bottle explodes.

In a recent development, in the wake of the 2020 wildfires, Shellhammer turned his attention to smoke-tainted hops. The primary culprit is volatile phenols (VP), which are produced when the lignin in plant cells is exposed to the high heat of a wildfire. Earlier this year, the OSU team discovered that smoke exposure while the hops are drying increased VP uptake and substantially altered the hops’ aroma; those with higher levels took on meaty, smoky, and artificial BBQ notes; medicinal flavors have also been reported. Those notes were so strong that they overpowered more desirable beery qualities, like citrus notes or aroma intensity.

For this latest project, Shellhammer worked with graduate student Cade Jobe to harvest Idaho-grown Cascade hops. Then they “smoked” the hops in kilns using wood pellets injected into the air intake systems, then dried them. They also harvested and dried non-smoked hops as a control.

Credit: Ellie Lafferty/Oregon State University Credit: Ellie Lafferty/Oregon State University.

In a recent development, next, Shellhammer and Jobe brewed several batches of beer, blending smoke-tainted hops with untainted hops at different levels (25,  50, and 75 percent), along with beer brewed using only tainted hops and beer brewed with no tainted hops. They did this using both a dry-hopping process and one where they added hops during wort boiling. They measured the VP concentrations of each batch of beer with gas chromatography. Finally, a panel of 24 blind tasters evaluated each beer.

In a recent development, shellhammer and Jobe found that dry-hopping with smoke-tainted hops resulted in increased VP concentrations; the more tainted hops were included, the higher those concentrations. The tasters reported more intense smoky aromas in those beers as well as meaty, smoky, medicinal, and artificial BBQ flavors.

By contrast, when tainted hops were added during the boil, the resulting beer was pretty much indistinguishable from beers brewed with no smoke-tainted hops, even though the former still showed the same increases in VP concentrations. There was no discernible difference when hops were added during the wort boiling stage.

According to recent reports, the authors suggest brewers could blend smoke-tainted hops with untainted batches when dry-hopping, keeping the smoke-tainted hops to less than 50 percent. This would still allow brewers to use tainted batches of hops, reducing the economic impact of wildfires on beer production.

In a recent development, “Hop growers and brewers are looking for guidance on whether and how to use smoke-affected hops,” said Jobe. “This research begins to provide some practical information to help hop growers and brewers understand how smoky hops impact beer so that they can make the best decisions.”.

According to recent reports, there’s still more research to be done to confirm the precise ratios and to replicate these initial findings. Future research should also explore the impact of hops exposed to smoke under field conditions, when the plant is still metabolically active, along with consumer studies to evaluate whether beer drinkers more generally will find the flavors of beers made with blended hops (tainted and untainted) acceptable. The findings may not extend to wine production, however, since the fermentation processes are so different, per the authors. And grapes comprise almost all the raw materials in wine, while hops are a smaller fraction of beer brewing ingredients.

Sources indicate that journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists, 2026. DOI: 10.1080/03610470.2026.2749166  (About DOIs).

  • Recent findings suggest that it's been less than a week since Grand Theft Auto 6 has been released, and it's surprising to see so much progress already being made.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Let the recompilation efforts begin.

It has been revealed that we still don't know when we'll get a true PC port of Grand Theft Auto 6 (rumors point to early next year), but that's not stopping developers from trying to make unofficial PC ports from happening. Separately, gamers have found a few ways to move beyond the game's 30 fps framerate cap, which makes everything look far more sluggish than modern 60 fps titles like the Ocarina of Time remake.

Recent findings suggest that it's been less than a week since Grand Theft Auto 6 has been released, and it's surprising to see so much progress already being made. When it comes to PC ports, Rockstar has already taken down the Discord server for the Leonida project, which reportedly got GTA 6 to successfully boot up. But Leonida isn't alone. The site "Port Watch VI" is right now tracking several recompilation efforts, and claims to have seen the leading project load the game and allow players to move and talk to NPCs "very slowly.".

Even though Rockstar will likely be quick to crack down, we'll likely see more ports spring up now that the hacking group Cyberleek has reportedly dumped files from GTA 6's Xbox build, as well as an executable that could help developers recompile the game.

There's a good chance that an unofficial GTA 6 PC release will arrive before Rockstar's official port. Modern game recompilation efforts are often helped by AI coding tools, and they focus specifically on making games work on PC hardware seamlessly, instead of emulating an entire console.

For people who have GTA 6 on the PS5, modders have already found ways to boost the game's perceived performance through the video enhancement tool Veyra and NVIDIA's DLSS 5, according to Videocardz. Running the PS5 version of the game through a 4K capture card, or via Sony's Remote Play feature, allows Veyra to apply frame generation and other DLSS 5 enhancements to go beyond the game's 30 fps console limit. It's not a perfect solution, though, since both frame generation, GPU enhancements and remote streaming all introduce significantly latency.

For Xbox GTA 6 players, an easy-to-perform glitch unlocks a 40fps version of the game, which should look noticeably smoother than the stock 30 fps. It's unclear how long that glitch will stick around, though, as it really is simple to do. Rockstar has confirmed that we won't be seeing an official 60 fps console mode because their CPUs aren't powerful enough to support simulating such a complex environment at higher frame rates.

  • Los Angeles-based Harbinger remarked Tuesday it secured more than $100 million in financing, including a convertible note from Pinegrove Venture Partners and senior debt from Erebor Bank, which introduced in February 2026 and recently surpassed $1 billion in loans, according to the Financial Times.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Harbinger has tapped Palmer Luckey’s Erebor Bank as a newly introduced source of capital as the electric truck startup looks to diversify how it funds its growth and an expanding portfolio of products spanning autonomous vehicles, energy storage, and defense.

Los Angeles-based Harbinger remarked Tuesday it secured more than $100 million in financing, including a convertible note from Pinegrove Venture Partners and senior debt from Erebor Bank, which introduced in February 2026 and recently surpassed $1 billion in loans, according to the Financial Times.

Recent findings suggest that the new financing comes less than three weeks after Harbinger raised $240 million in a Series D funding round co-led by Tiger Global, Capricorn’s Technology Impact Fund, and Ridgeline. FedEx, which ordered 2,000 trucks from Harbinger, also participated.

It has been revealed that harbinger co-founder and chief executive John Harris explained in a statement that building an industrial technology manufacturer at scale requires a “different financing approach,” adding that the capital needed to ramp up production and deliver vehicles to customers shouldn’t have to come entirely from equity. Harris noted that major vehicle and aerospace manufacturers have long relied on debt financing to support their production operations.

Erebor is now Harbinger’s primary banking partner. In a statement, Luckey said traditional lenders have struggled to support the unique capital needs of businesses developing real technology and creating U.S. jobs.

“Harbinger is exactly the kind of business we built Erebor to back: an American manufacturer building world-class technology,” he said.

US plans newly introduced tariffs on EU, China and 12 others

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (757 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The United States on Wednesday proposed upcoming tariffs of up to 20% on imports from 14 economies, including the European Union and China.
  • The Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR) unveiled the proposed duties after completing an eight-month investigation into alleged unfair trade practices involving 16 trading partners.
  • Washington accuses the targeted economies of promoting excessive industrial production, allowing cheaper goods to undercut American manufacturers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The United States on Wednesday proposed upcoming tariffs of up to 20% on imports from 14 economies, including the European Union and China.

The Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR) unveiled the proposed duties after completing an eight-month investigation into alleged unfair trade practices involving 16 trading partners.

Washington accuses the targeted economies of promoting excessive industrial production, allowing cheaper goods to undercut American manufacturers.

According to recent reports, the proposed tariffs largely stick to rates set under existing trade agreements, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC on Wednesday. However, he added that some rates could be "topped up" by a few percentage points.

The duties will be subject to a public comment period and a hearing before taking effect, possibly in January at the earliest.

China would face an additional tariff of 20%, the joint-highest rate among the targeted economies.

The proposed duties would respect the 15% tariff cap agreed with the European Union, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, as well as the 19% cap agreed with Malaysia, a senior US administration official said.

Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Singapore, Switzerland, Thailand and Vietnam would also be affected.

Mexico and Norway are currently excluded from the proposed measures. Greer stated talks with Mexico were continuing as Washington's investigation into its trade practices remained ongoing.

In a separate announcement, the USTR also proposed higher tariffs on Brazilian raw and refined sugar and a new 10% duty on aircraft, which would affect Brazilian manufacturer Embraer.

The senior US official said the proposed duties would not exceed tariff limits negotiated under existing trade agreements.

However, the new tariffs on China would be added to duties of around 25% imposed during Trump's first term, bringing the combined rate for some Chinese goods to 45%.

Around $30 billion worth of Chinese imports that Washington is considering for tariff reductions would be exempt from the fresh measures.

The proposed duties would not be added to existing sector-specific tariffs on products such as automobiles, steel and aluminum.

Industry observers note that nor would they be combined with tariffs of between 10% and 12.5% imposed in July against 60 trading partners over alleged insufficient action against forced labor. Where both measures apply, the higher rate would prevail.

The European Union stated on Wednesday it would examine the proposed US tariffs but rejected Washington's allegations of excessive industrial production.

"We strongly reject the premise that Europe is a source of structural overcapacity," the EU stated, adding that it expected Washington to honor the trade agreement reached with Brussels last year.

Beijing also rejected Washington's allegations of excessive industrial production and reiterated its opposition to trade wars, but stopped short of threatening retaliation.

"The so-called 'overcapacity' is a false matter, and China opposes using it as an excuse for political manipulation," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Washington has accused Beijing of flooding global markets with cheap exports, ranging from steel to electric vehicles and solar products.

Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping last week in Shenzhen and is due to host him at the G20 summit in Miami in December.

It has been revealed that an existing trade truce between Washington and Beijing is set to expire on January 10. Access to rare earth minerals and Chinese purchases of US agricultural products could feature in further negotiations.

The measures are intended in part to replace revenues lost after the US Supreme Court struck down Trump's sweeping global tariffs in February.

The court ruled that Trump lacked the authority to impose the duties by declaring an economic emergency and bypassing Congress.

The newly introduced measures instead rely on Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows Washington to investigate and retaliate against unfair or discriminatory foreign trade practices.

Trump has repeatedly promised that tariffs will bring manufacturing jobs back to the US and reduce the federal deficit.

The proposed duties could put further pressure on American businesses, which may pass additional costs on to consumers.

US consumer inflation reached 3.7% year-on-year in September, close to a three-year high. Earlier tariffs, the effects of Trump's war on Iran and a boom in artificial intelligence investment have contributed to rising prices.

High living costs were a key concern in November's midterm elections, which saw Trump's Republican Party lose control of both chambers of Congress.

A Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted after the elections found that 62% of respondents supported efforts to repeal Trump's tariffs.

This underrated Pixel feature is more versatile than you realize

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (984 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you're not using this feature, you're missing out on a lot of convenience.
  • Recent findings suggest that if you own a Pixel phone, you probably look forward to the upcoming features that pop up after an Android OS enhancement and Pixel Drop.
  • But there's one old, reliable and underrated feature that you may have missed, and it's actually quite versatile and convenient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're not using this feature, you're missing out on a lot of convenience.

Recent findings suggest that if you own a Pixel phone, you probably look forward to the upcoming features that pop up after an Android OS enhancement and Pixel Drop. The latest Android 17 QPR2 and the November 2026 Pixel Drop, for example, upgraded Pixel Search and added cool customizable icon designs, Transit Mode for train commuters, Pixel VIPs real-time location sharing and a new Status bar settings menu for all Pixel 6a and newer phones, plus expanded Gemini Intelligence, Extreme Charging Mode and other features for the Pixel 10 and 11.

But there's one old, reliable and underrated feature that you may have missed, and it's actually quite versatile and convenient. It's called Quick Tap, and it transforms the back of your Pixel phone into a customizable shortcut when you tap it twice. Quick Tap allows you to accomplish common tasks with just one hand and without scrolling through any menus.

According to recent reports, the Quick Tap feature is available on all Pixel 4a (5G) and newer phones. To access it and to customize the settings, open the Settings app on your Pixel phone, then tap System > Gestures > Quick Tap to start actions.

From there, you can then choose a built-in action for Quick Tap to perform when you double-tap the back of your phone. All of these actions are pretty convenient, but since Quick Tap only supports one action at a time, you should choose the one you're likely to use most.

You can assign Quick Tap to turn the flashlight on and off even when your phone is locked. Or set the feature to take a screenshot without having to hold the power and volume-down buttons at the same time. Quick Tap can also play or pause music, videos or podcasts using just about any of your favorite streaming apps with just a couple of taps. This is super convenient when you want to watch or listen to content while you're driving, cooking or working out, because you don't need to unlock the phone, navigate the apps and resume your media. Just double-tap the back of your Pixel.

It has been revealed that use Quick Tap to wake up Gemini without having to talk to the phone. Or assign Quick Tap to easily show notifications without having to pull the notification shade down from the top of the screen; Quick Tap pulls it down for you. You can also use the feature to open the multiple app overview screen and switch between recently used apps without navigating. Quick Tap can also launch any app installed on your Pixel phone — you just need to assign which app you use most.

One thing to consider: Quick Tap works perfectly on a naked Pixel phone. However, if you have a protective case on your phone, you might need to try a few things to get it working as it should. If your Pixel phone case is super thick, finger tapping may not be enough to get it going. Lighter-weight cases, though, should allow you to activate Quick Tap without much effort.

Sources indicate that if you're having trouble, there is an option within the Quick Tap settings called Require stronger taps, designed to prevent accidental triggering of an app when you put the phone down or slide it into your pocket. Make sure that's turned off and then test it out. Messing around with where you tap your phone can also help. If you have a magnetic accessory on the back of the phone, keep tapping around until you find the sweet spot. For the foldable Pixel 9 Pro Fold and Pixel 11 Pro Fold phones, you can tap the rear glass panel whether the phone is unfolded or closed to activate Quick Tap.

Quick Tap can be paired with other apps and automation tools to get even more out of the feature. The Tap, Tap app can be used to supplement Quick Tap by providing support for both double-taps and triple-taps, so you can assign more than one action and choose from a wider range of over 50 available actions to assign. You could also connect Quick Tap to a free pop-up menu or folder app so the double-tap triggers a menu of your most-used apps or tools.

Your Pixel phone is also loaded with built-in Gestures, which give you another way to access certain tools and features without having to unlock or swipe — or install another app like Tap, Tap. To find these, go to Settings > System > Gestures.

It has been revealed that let's say you want to use your Quick Tap action to toggle the flashlight when you double-tap the phone, but you also want fast access to your camera or Google Wallet. You can do this by customizing your Gestures to open either the camera or Google Wallet by double-pressing the power button. You can also press and hold the power button to summon Gemini. Then there's the Flip to Shhh feature that automatically enables Do Not Disturb when you place your Pixel phone facedown, as well as a shortcut that lets you tap or lift your phone to check the time, notifications and other info.

Sources indicate that between Quick Tap and Gestures, your Pixel phone is versatile enough to let you simply tap or press your way through a bunch of actions to maximize convenience and one-handed operation. That makes day-to-day phone use much more convenient. Assign it to your smart home device app for quick controllability, or have it open Google Wallet to quickly pay when you're at the store, for example. Anyone who uses a phone knows it's a whole lot easier to tap the phone than to unlock it or swipe through apps... especially if you only have one hand available.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A European Ariane 6 launcher propelled 36 satellites into orbit for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation Tuesday, continuing the network’s build-out after 40 satellites were lost earlier this month during a failure of United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket.

Sources indicate that the launch was an notable rebound for Amazon, bringing the Amazon Leo fleet to 432 satellites as the manufacturer seeks to fill the void left by the grounding of ULA’s Vulcan rocket, Amazon’s primary launch provider. Now, an Amazon official tells Ars it is accelerating several Falcon 9 launches the company has purchased from SpaceX, which also owns the Starlink satellite network that Amazon seeks to dethrone.

It has been revealed that the next Falcon 9 launch for Amazon Leo is now planned for December, Amazon mentioned, moved forward from its previous launch date next year. Several more Falcon 9s are scheduled to launch Amazon Leo satellites in rapid succession after the December flight.

Amazon cast a wide net when it started signing deals for launch services five years ago, securing rides on 108 flights with every available medium- or heavy-lift rocket in the West to place a fleet of 3,232 satellites into low-Earth orbit. As of Tuesday, Amazon and its launch partners have completed 17 of those flights, with one mission failure.

Amazon executives initially bought up capacity from US-based United Launch Alliance, Europe’s Arianespace, and Blue Origin. Nearly all of those launch contracts depended on rockets still in development: ULA’s Vulcan, Europe’s Ariane 6, and Blue Origin’s New Glenn.

According to recent reports, each launch vehicle faced development delays, as all latest rockets do. New Glenn has been grounded since May after an explosion on Blue Origin’s launch pad in Florida. ULA’s Vulcan will be sidelined for months after misfiring during a mission with Amazon satellites on November 15.

Amazon started booking introduces in 2023 with SpaceX. Falcon 9 successfully launched Amazon’s first three missions last year, each with 24 satellites. Amazon soon reserved 10 more flights on SpaceX’s Falcon 9 rocket as delays mounted with Amazon Leo’s other launch providers, especially ULA and Blue Origin.

Industry observers note that the relationship between Amazon and SpaceX is a peculiar one. Amazon aims to catch up to SpaceX’s Starlink network, now boasting more than 11,000 satellites, to bring competition to the satellite broadband market. Federal regulators approved Amazon Leo’s second-generation constellation earlier this year, an addition that will bring the fleet to more than 7,000 satellites in the 2030s. Amazon also prepares a direct-to-device service, joining SpaceX and others in the pursuit of consumer demand for mobile connectivity.

According to recent reports, but Starlink is far ahead. SpaceX has repurposed the Starlink satellite design for use on several US military programs, and Starlink rolls out on Falcon 9 are winding down as SpaceX’s Starship enters service. Starship is capable of launching heavier, more powerful Starlink satellites, a culmination that will only widen the gap with Amazon and other competitors in the satellite Internet business.

Starlink’s move to Starship opens up launch slots on Falcon 9, allowing Amazon to accelerate its rolls out with SpaceX in the near term. But SpaceX doesn’t proposal to keep Falcon 9 around for long. The firm has reportedly stopped accepting commercial Falcon 9 bookings after 2028.

Industry observers note that that means Amazon Leo needs its other launch providers to step up. Arianespace is doing so, with four successful Ariane 6 flights for Amazon this year. Amazon reserved six additional flights with Arianespace in September as Ariane 6 proved its mettle.

But there are questions about Europe’s ability to ramp up production of Ariane 6 rockets, which are single-use and not reusable like Falcon 9 and Upcoming Glenn. Europe’s rocket factories are sized to support a launch cadence of up to nine or 10 Ariane 6 flights per year. Arianespace will likely reach six Ariane 6 flights this year, with one more remaining before the end of December.

European taxpayers paid for development of the Ariane 6 and the industrial capacity to build the rockets, and they continue to subsidize each Ariane 6 flight, whether it carries a European government payload or commercial satellites for a large American corporation like Amazon.

In a recent development, european government ministers are mulling proposals to increase Ariane 6 production to meet surging demand from commercial users and Europe’s internal space programs. A decision could come next month, but a ramp-up in launch cadence won’t happen overnight.

Amazon paid United Launch Alliance hundreds of millions of dollars for expansion at Cape Canaveral, Florida, to prepare for as many as 25 Vulcan introduces per year. Such a launch cadence is a long way off for ULA, which has now released Vulcan five times (with one failure) in its three years of service.

It has been revealed that blue Origin, owned by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, could resume New Glenn flights early next year after completing a launch pad rebuild. It is not clear when Amazon might begin launching on New Glenn, but finding slots in the rocket’s launch schedule could be difficult as Blue Origin prioritizes work for NASA’s Artemis lunar program.

It has been revealed that in the meantime, SpaceX will offer Amazon its most assured rides to space. Falcon 9s can launch from Cape Canaveral every few days, and Amazon is ready to tap into that capability with hundreds of satellites in storage waiting to go to orbit.

A funeral was held earlier in southern Gaza for three Palestinians killed in an Israeli strike.

At least seven Palestinians, including a senior Hamas security official, have been killed in Israeli air strikes in the Gaza Strip, health officials and first responders say.

Recent findings suggest that naeem Abu Nahel, the head of Hamas's internal security service, was targeted in western Gaza City, Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry said. The 50-year-old had only been in the position since September, when his predecessor was captured in a raid by Israeli special forces.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz confirmed that Abu Nahel was "eliminated" by the Israeli military.

The six other people were killed in two earlier air strikes elsewhere in Gaza.

Three people, including a teenage boy, were killed in the Wadi Gaza area, south of Gaza City, according to the health officials and first responders. The other three were killed at a police station in the al-Mawasi area, west of Khan Younis, they added.

According to recent reports, gaza's police force, which operates under the interior ministry, remarked two of its officers were among those who died in the second attack. It also accused Israel of "an ongoing campaign targeting the police apparatus aimed at sowing chaos" in the territory.

The Israeli military said it struck "military operatives" in both areas.

Witnesses said an Israeli drone targeted Naeem Abu Nahel as he was walking on a side street near a tent camp for displaced people in Gaza City.

Several other people were reportedly seriously injured in the strike.

The Israeli military remarked Abu Nahel had "possessed extensive institutional knowledge" about Hamas's internal security service - which is responsible for enforcing discipline, protecting infrastructure and rooting out informants - and that his death constituted "a blow to the apparatus's management capabilities".

It also alleged that he had advanced attacks on Israeli troops and civilians during the war and that it killed him "to remove the threat he posed".

Gaza's interior ministry stated Abu Nahel's killing followed what it described as the internal security service's "vital achievements in combating gangs collaborating with the occupation [Israel] and operating in areas under the control of its military".

Gaza's health ministry warned that there was a rapid rise in cases of meningitis in October.

Violence has continued in Gaza since Israel and Hamas agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire in October last year. Israeli strikes take place almost daily in areas under Hamas's control, which are home to 2.1 million people, most of them displaced.

At least 1,679 people have been killed in Gaza over the past 13 months, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Israel notes six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza during the same period.

The humanitarian situation also remains dire, with heavy rainfall earlier this month causing flooding and damage to thousands of shelters for displaced families.

The UN and its partners have called on Israel - which controls Gaza's crossings - to allow in more supplies to help Palestinians prepare for the winter, including tents, heaters and water pumps, as well as vaccines and medicines to combat infectious diseases.

On Tuesday, the health ministry warned that there had been a rapid rise in cases of meningitis, with 272 reported in October - about eight times the usual monthly average.

Fifteen deaths had been attributed to the infection so far this year, including five reported between August and October, it stated.

Israeli military body Cogat said on Monday it was "working to provide a dedicated humanitarian response" and that a newly approved package of pumps, generators, water tankers and medical equipment had been presented at a meeting with UN agencies.

The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It may have taken 15 years for Instagram to launch on the iPad, but Instagram’s other app, Threads, has taken a slightly faster path to the Apple tablet. In an overnight revision, the company rolled out a massive-screen version of the X competitor. It’s also added another latest feature, borrowed from X: the stock-tracking feature known as cashtags.

In a recent development, while the iPad version of the app works well in portrait orientation, some users are disappointed to find that the landscape layout doesn’t work as they’d expect. Instead of offering a multi-column interface as on Threads’ web app, the iPad app focuses on the user’s main feed in a single-column layout. There are also options to swipe right and left from the main screen to access the search screen and the feeds menu, respectively.

The iPad app isn’t the organization’s only update in the latest release. According to a post from Threads engineer Guy Dickinson, Threads will now support cashtags — a feature popularized by Twitter years ago for tracking live stock information. These specialized tags start with the dollar sign (“$”) followed by a ticker symbol. When you click on a cashtag, you can follow the discussions around the stock.

It has been revealed that in addition, Threads is adding live stock quotes, charts, and other context at the top of each cashtag’s page. As you search for a particular cashtag, the autocomplete search results will display the stock’s current price and the percentage it’s up or down. Dickinson says the feature will currently support NYSE and Nasdaq stocks, ETFs, and crypto. Cashtags will be supported on the web, iOS, and Android. However, they’re just now rolling out, so you may not immediately see them.

Sources indicate that the update points to Threads’ broader ambition to compete with X, not only as a destination for discussions about various topics, but also as a place where people can track real-time news and information. Cashtags in particular could attract traders and investors to Threads who typically rely on X.

Despite facing stiff competition from X, Meta confirmed earlier this year that Threads topped 500 million monthly users, and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg indicates the company believes the app is on track to reach a billion users over time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The manufacturer is already barred from US sales, but the verdict could cost it billions in penalties.
  • It has been revealed that huawei Technologies has been found guilty of bank fraud and conspiracy to steal trade secrets by a US jury, the Associated Press reports.
  • According to recent reports, racketeering is traditionally reserved for organized criminal acts — the kind often associated with the Mafia, for example — but the AP writes US prosecutors thought the charge could apply to what they described as Huawei's repeated theft of intellectual property and trade secrets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The manufacturer is already barred from US sales, but the verdict could cost it billions in penalties.

It has been revealed that huawei Technologies has been found guilty of bank fraud and conspiracy to steal trade secrets by a US jury, the Associated Press reports. The verdict is the result of charges brought by the Department of Justice in 2019, though the jury acquitted Huawei of racketeering conspiracy, as well as conspiracy to obstruct justice.

According to recent reports, racketeering is traditionally reserved for organized criminal acts — the kind often associated with the Mafia, for example — but the AP writes US prosecutors thought the charge could apply to what they described as Huawei's repeated theft of intellectual property and trade secrets. The company has been accused of copying or outright stealing from competitors in the past, and the DOJ pointed to Huawei's sale of routers with code copied from a competitor as evidence. Prosecutors also accused Huawei of violating US sanctions by selling equipment to Iran and North Korea, and misleading banks and officials to hide it.

In a statement, Huawei welcomed its acquittal on the racketeering charge, saying it lacked "factual basis.".

"We believe the government's remaining charges are equally without legal or factual merit," the company continued. "The five trade secret-related disputes cited by the government were all civil matters that were resolved over the past two decades. No court ever found Huawei liable for willful intellectual property misappropriation, and the company was never ordered to pay damages for trade secret misappropriation. We will thoroughly review the relevant verdicts and take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests." Huawei attorney Brian Heberlig told AP the company planned to appeal its convictions.

In a recent development, huawei isn't allowed to sell its products in the US due to its placement on the Federal Communications Commission's Covered List, so outside of the possibility of paying "billions of dollars in penalties," per the AP, it's not clear how these charges will impact its business. In 2025, the FCC opened an investigation into whether Huawei and fellow Chinese companies ZTE and China Telecom were circumventing those restrictions, so the tech giant could face even more scrutiny in the US soon.

#116822. Blade Runner 2099 finally takes this franchise to the stars
